## About

This page documents Rick Gilmore's work related to completing Exercise 04 for PSYCH 490.007 in Fall 2026.

The assignment involves choosing an existing dataset and making at least three (3) visualizations using the *ggplot2* package.
For each figure, I am to write a short summary of the question I intend to ask with the figure, and how the visualization I generate answers or doesn't answer the question.
If my figure doesn't clearly answer the question, then I should explain how the figure might be improved or clarified to do so.
This critique could include a suggestion to use a different type of figure.

## Setup

```{r}
#| label: setup
library(ggplot2)
library(nflreadr)
```

## Explore datasets

```{r}
data()
```

I chose to use the *schedules* dataset from the *nflreadr* package.

## Load dataset

```{r}
nfl_scheds <- load_schedules() # nflreadr
```

Using `summary(nfl_scheds)`, I discover that the dataset has the following variables:

```{r}
summary(nfl_scheds)
```

### Make figures

## Figure 1

This figure shows a violin plot of home team scores. It should show whether there is a modal (most common) value.

```{r}
#| label: fig-ex-04-01
nfl_scheds |>
  ggplot() +
  aes(x = home_score) +
  geom_violin()
```

The violin shape is widest between 20 and about 25, indicating that scores in this range are the most common.

I could confirm this with the following R code:

```{r}
with(nfl_scheds, summary(home_score))
```

Sure enough, the mean is 23.3 and the median 23.

## Figure 2

For Figure 2, I decided to try to plot my own version of a figure I linked to in Exercise 02.

Here is the figure from Exercise 02:

![Figure 1 from https://www.psychologicalscience.org/redesign/wp-content/uploads/2015/12/TCD_fig_1.jpg](https://www.psychologicalscience.org/redesign/wp-content/uploads/2015/12/TCD_fig_1.jpg){#fig-ex-01}

Here is the figure I made:

```{r}
#| label: fig-ex-04-02
#| fig-cap: "Rengenerating Figure 1 from https://www.psychologicalscience.org/redesign/wp-content/uploads/2015/12/TCD_fig_1.jpg"
age <- seq(from=3, to = 18)
mean_t <- c(54, 54, 54, 52, 51, 50.5, 49.5, 49, 48, 47.5, 47.25, 46, 45, 44.5, 44, 45)
sex = rep("male", length(age))

activity <- data.frame(age, mean_t)

activity |>
  ggplot() +
  aes(x = age, y = mean_t, color = sex) +
  geom_line()
```

Note that I only show the male data.
I had to enter the data by hand, and I got tired of that.
You get the general idea.
